section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Tangent Line Intuition (1 min)
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of using a tangent line to approximate the root of a function. Visualize a curve $f(x)$ and show how starting from a point $x_0$, the tangent line intersects the x-axis at $x_1$, which is closer to the true root.
section_1.example: Imagine a robot attempting to land on a specific target (the root) on a platform. It adjusts its position by 'sliding' down the slope of the terrain at its current location.

section_2.title: The Newton-Raphson Iteration Formula (1 min)
section_2.content: Derive the mathematical iteration formula: $x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n) / f'(x_n)$. Emphasize that this is an iterative process where we refine our guess step-by-step.
section_2.example: Use a ball rolling on a landscape. The derivative represents the slope; the ball rolls faster where the slope is steep and slows down as it approaches the flat 'valley floor' (the root).

section_3.title: From 1D Roots to Complex Planes (1 min)
section_3.content: Transition from real numbers to the complex plane $\mathbb{C}$. Explain that when we solve $f(z) = z^n - 1 = 0$ for complex numbers, there are multiple roots (e.g., the roots of unity).
section_3.example: A multi-colored beacon system: If a signal starts at point $z_0$, which 'root beacon' will it eventually be pulled into? Color-code the starting points based on the final root they converge to.

section_4.title: Visualizing Newton Fractals (1.5 mins)
section_4.content: Explain how sensitive the convergence is to the starting point. When we map each starting point to a color based on which root it reaches, complex, infinite boundaries emerge—this is the Newton Fractal.
section_4.example: Show an animation where zooming into the boundary between two colors reveals repeating, self-similar patterns—just like a coastline that remains jagged no matter how closely you look.

section_5.title: Summary and Conclusion (0.5 mins)
section_5.content: Recap: Newton's method is a simple root-finding tool; when applied to the complex plane, it creates profound fractal beauty. Emphasize that the chaos at the boundaries is a signature of nonlinear dynamics.
section_5.example: Final shot: A high-resolution Newton Fractal generated from the function $f(z) = z^3 - 1$, showing three distinct basins of attraction.
